name: Ruxolitinib cream
lead: Ruxolitinib cream (brand name Opzelura) is a topical Janus kinase (JAK1/JAK2) inhibitor. The US FDA approved it in September 2021 for mild to moderate atopic dermatitis, described as the first topical JAK inhibitor approved in the US, and in July 2022 for vitiligo.[1] Its appearance relevance lies mainly in vitiligo, an autoimmune condition that causes skin depigmentation.[2]

Two phase 3 trials published in 2022 tested it in nonsegmental vitiligo,[2] and two phase 3 trials in 2021 tested it in atopic dermatitis.[3] Trials in other skin conditions are registered or completed.[4][5]

paras: Medical uses are atopic dermatitis and nonsegmental vitiligo.[1] Cosmetic relevance is through repigmentation in vitiligo.[2]

Ruxolitinib inhibits JAK1 and JAK2, interfering with JAK-STAT signaling that affects gene expression in inflammatory and autoimmune processes.[1] A pharmacokinetic analysis from phase 2 and 3 trials examined systemic exposure in atopic dermatitis.[6]

A phase 2 randomized trial in vitiligo reported results to 52 weeks of double-blind treatment, with the cream investigated as the first potential approved repigmentation therapy.[7] Two phase 3 vehicle-controlled trials (TRuE-V1 and TRuE-V2) in people aged 12 and over with nonsegmental vitiligo were published in the New England Journal of Medicine in 2022.[2] For atopic dermatitis, two phase 3 trials evaluated 8-week efficacy and safety,[3] a phase 2 study compared the cream with triamcinolone cream,[8] and long-term phase 3 safety data have been published.[9] Registered studies also cover genital vitiligo, prurigo nodularis, lichen planus, lichen sclerosus and hidradenitis suppurativa.[10][11][12][13][14]

The cream's own adverse-effect profile is detailed in trial reports and the product label.[2][3] Oral JAK inhibitors carry warnings about infections, low blood counts and other laboratory abnormalities.[1]

timeline.event: Phase 2 vitiligo trial published in the Lancet.[7]
FDA approves the cream for atopic dermatitis.[1]
FDA approves it for vitiligo; phase 3 vitiligo trials published.[1][2]

card.summary: A prescription JAK-inhibitor cream approved for vitiligo repigmentation and eczema, backed by phase 3 trials.
card.note: Prescription-only; oral JAK inhibitors carry serious-infection warnings.

quick.overview:
Ruxolitinib cream (Opzelura) is a topical JAK inhibitor approved in the US for atopic dermatitis (2021) and vitiligo (2022).

For vitiligo it has phase 2 and two phase 3 randomized trials behind it, making it one of the better-studied treatments for skin repigmentation.
quick.mechanism: It inhibits JAK1 and JAK2 enzymes, damping the immune signaling involved in vitiligo and eczema.
quick.risks: Prescription only. Specific adverse events are listed in trial reports and the label; oral JAK inhibitors carry warnings on infections and blood counts.
